blocks.text:
Natural-Speed Listening & Implication
เป้าหมาย: ติดตามคำพูดต่อเนื่องที่มีการแทรก แก้คำ และสงวนท่าที

Use the language of natural-speed listening & implication to complete the unit's practical or interpretive task.
Identify and relay the essential information in the two readings without adding unsupported facts.
Respond to the two listening scripts with appropriate clarification and source-sensitive wording.

Reading A
A planning transcript reads, 'We have the funding—well, the first instalment—and we should be able to start next month, assuming recruitment goes to plan.' An inattentive summary turns this into a fully funded project starting next month. The repair narrows the funding claim, while should and assuming qualify the schedule. In natural speech, such information may appear in brief insertions rather than neatly separated sentences. A listener must maintain a provisional interpretation and update it as the turn develops. Familiarity with conversational rhythm helps, but interpreting dense speech also requires conceptual attention to scope, source and the distinction between a forecast and a commitment.

Read for purpose, then locate the people, events, conditions and limits. Track stance, scope and evidential status across sources. Distinguish concession from endorsement and implication from explicit assertion. Synthesize by issue, retaining unresolved disagreement. Adapt density and register to the reader without changing commitments.

Reading B
Written clarification: First instalment received. Later payments depend on milestones. Recruitment remains open. The proposed start date is a forecast, not an authorised public announcement. The transcript and clarification should be read together.

Compare the two inputs: what is shared, what is additional, and what is not known? Use only details actually supplied. All characters, organisations, figures and events in these inputs are fictional classroom materials.

self-repair
หน้าที่: อัปเดตขอบเขตคำกล่าว
Model: We have the funding—well, the first instalment.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

should be able to
หน้าที่: คาดการณ์แบบไม่รับประกัน
Model: We should be able to start next month.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

not with every detail
หน้าที่: แยกเห็นด้วยภาพรวมจากทั้งหมด
Model: I support the direction, not every detail.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

Guided practice: cover the word bank, reconstruct five target expressions, and explain their meaning in these particular contexts. Then use two in a new example. The same word may have a different sense elsewhere.

Listening script A — authored script; recorded audio and human audio QC are pending. Reading the transcript is text-based preparation, not evidence of independent listening ability.

A: So we're fully funded and starting next month?
B: Not fully funded—the first instalment is in. And next month is still conditional on recruitment.
A: I'll separate confirmed funding from the forecast date.
B: Please do; the public notice has not been authorised.

Listening script B
I am broadly comfortable with the direction, though not, I should stress, with every detail. The access plan needs work. If we resolve that, I can support a pilot. I would not describe this as approval for a full rollout.

First pass: identify purpose and main message. Second pass: note essential details and any corrections. Check against the script only after the listening attempt when approved audio becomes available. For now, practise with a teacher or partner reading the script.

Pronunciation and prosody
Shape long turns into coherent rhetorical units. Use prominence and pauses to mark qualification, reformulation and source shifts. Intonation can suggest stance but is not conclusive evidence of intention by itself.

Interaction rehearsal: take both roles. Ask one clarification question, answer it using the source, and check that the other person has understood. Do not equate quietness, accent or hesitation with lack of ability.

Unit transfer task
ติดตามคำพูดต่อเนื่องที่มีการแทรก แก้คำ และสงวนท่าที

Prepare a 240–320-word response and a 180–240-second spoken response using the unit inputs. Handle extended, implicit and professionally situated discourse with flexible register, coherent synthesis and precise qualification.

Planning sequence
1. Identify audience and purpose.
2. Select source details that the audience needs.
3. Mark any uncertainty, unconfirmed arrangement or missing information.
4. Choose two language features from Lesson 2.
5. Produce the response, then check meaning before surface accuracy.

Mediation: explain the essential information to a Thai-speaking classmate who has not read the sources. Preserve dates, quantities, conditions, agency and uncertainty. Say what cannot be concluded.

Online interaction: respond to a request for clarification, then add a follow-up checking question. Acknowledge corrections and revise your message where needed.

Quick review

should be able to: We should be able to start next month.
not with every detail: I support the direction, not every detail.
รักษาขอบเขตและระดับความมั่นใจของต้นฉบับ วิเคราะห์สิ่งที่กล่าวชัดกับสิ่งที่สื่อโดยนัย สังเคราะห์ตามประเด็นแทนเรียงย่อทีละแหล่ง

Self-check: Did I meet the purpose? Which source supports each factual detail? Did I make a suggestion sound confirmed? Can the other person act or understand appropriately? Which error should I revisit tomorrow?

inputs.label: Reading A
inputs.text: A planning transcript reads, 'We have the funding—well, the first instalment—and we should be able to start next month, assuming recruitment goes to plan.' An inattentive summary turns this into a fully funded project starting next month. The repair narrows the funding claim, while should and assuming qualify the schedule. In natural speech, such information may appear in brief insertions rather than neatly separated sentences. A listener must maintain a provisional interpretation and update it as the turn develops. Familiarity with conversational rhythm helps, but interpreting dense speech also requires conceptual attention to scope, source and the distinction between a forecast and a commitment.

inputs.label: Reading B
inputs.text: Written clarification: First instalment received. Later payments depend on milestones. Recruitment remains open. The proposed start date is a forecast, not an authorised public announcement. The transcript and clarification should be read together.

inputs.label: Listening script A
inputs.text:
A: So we're fully funded and starting next month?
B: Not fully funded—the first instalment is in. And next month is still conditional on recruitment.
A: I'll separate confirmed funding from the forecast date.
B: Please do; the public notice has not been authorised.

inputs.label: Listening script B
inputs.text: I am broadly comfortable with the direction, though not, I should stress, with every detail. The access plan needs work. If we resolve that, I can support a pilot. I would not describe this as approval for a full rollout.

pronunciation: Shape long turns into coherent rhetorical units. Use prominence and pauses to mark qualification, reformulation and source shifts. Intonation can suggest stance but is not conclusive evidence of intention by itself.

rubric.descriptors:
Target C1: Handle extended, implicit and professionally situated discourse with flexible register, coherent synthesis and precise qualification.
4 — Fully achieves the specified purpose with precise relevant detail, coherent organisation and effective control at this target level.
3 — Achieves the main purpose; minor omissions or language lapses do not materially distort meaning.
2 — Partially achieves the purpose; important detail, organisation or language needs revision.
1 — Limited assessable evidence; major gaps or distortion impede the task.
0 — No assessable response or wholly unrelated response.
Rate each dimension separately. For mediation, invented facts, erased conditions or reversed agency prevent a high fidelity score. Do not penalise an accent or a defensible alternative phrasing. Scores describe this task only, not certified CEFR attainment.

retrieval.prompt: Without notes: recall 2 target expressions from Natural-Speed Listening & Implication; explain one source detail and use self-repair in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 3 target expressions from Natural-Speed Listening & Implication; explain one source detail and use should be able to in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 4 target expressions from Natural-Speed Listening & Implication; explain one source detail and use not with every detail in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 5 target expressions from Natural-Speed Listening & Implication; explain one source detail and use self-repair in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.

remediation.action: Return to Readings A/B; underline the evidence for your statement, restore any lost condition, and say explicitly what remains unknown. Retry Q-C1-09-015 and the mediation task.
Revisit the three Lesson 2 models. Identify the intended function, correct the form, and produce a new example. Retrieve the missed expression again after one day.

masteryCheck.decision: Record evidence by construct; no pass mark or CEFR certification without human standard setting.
